sources.entry: Pocket ID | Simple OIDC provider that uses passkeys for authentication

summary.one_liner: Pocket ID is a self-hosted OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 provider that lets users sign in to their applications using only passkeys, with no passwords.
summary.what_it_does: Pocket ID acts as an OpenID Connect Certified and OAuth 2.0 provider, so applications can delegate sign-in to it. It supports passkey authentication exclusively, meaning users do not set or use passwords. The README describes it as deliberately simpler than alternatives like Keycloak or ORY Hydra, aimed at simple use cases. It can be used with hardware security keys such as a Yubikey to sign in to self-hosted services. The README points to external documentation for the setup guide and further information. It is also listed under the Security category of the awesome-selfhost-docker list.
use_cases: OIDC provider for home lab apps
replacing Keycloak for simple SSO needs
OAuth 2.0 authorization server for internal apps
how_to_run: Use Docker (the README's recommended setup method)
Follow the setup guide in the project's documentation
notable: Passkey-only authentication with no password option
OpenID Connect Certified and OAuth 2.0 provider
Deliberately simpler alternative to Keycloak and ORY Hydra
Hardware security key support such as Yubikey, per the README
caveats: Passkey-only sign-in may not suit users who prefer passwords, as the README acknowledges some people may dislike the idea
README gives little detail on setup; it defers to external documentation
